- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% relative to prior high.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days — cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days, model underestimates downward trend — add 2–5% to forecast to account for mean reversion bias.
- Model frequently overestimates short-term (1–3 day) volatility — smooth 3-day moving average of forecast to reduce noise.
- When sentiment turns positive after negative streak (e.g., -0.7 → +0.3), model delays reaction — forecast should rise 1–2 days ahead of true sentiment shift.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) price action — adjust final 5–7 days upward by 3–8% if sentiment is positive or neutral.
